rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the key uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only baseline is already informative and how strong the unimodal signal is. This tests the minimal RNA-only, single-profile PCA configuration, giving a clean reference for later isolating the effects of multiprofile aggregation and multimodal fusion. It is the best first experiment because it is simple, low-risk, and provides the baseline needed to interpret more complex configurations efficiently.

The only completed result is an RNA-only PCA single-profile baseline with validation accuracy 0.485 and F1 0.464, leaving the value of the image modality completely untested. This experiment tests whether a simple image-only ResNet50 single-profile model is competitive, establishing a key modality baseline. It is the best next step because it reduces major uncertainty about whether image features should be pursued or combined with RNA, while avoiding confounds from multiprofile aggregation and fusion under a limited budget.

The only strong result so far is RNA-only PCA single-profile (0.485 acc), while image-only ResNet is much weaker (0.208 acc), so the main uncertainty is whether the promising RNA branch can be improved by using multiple profiles with a simple aggregation. config_002 keeps the same PCA encoder and tests multiprofile with avgpool, avoiding simultaneous changes to representation, transformer aggregation, or fusion. This is the best next experiment because it extends the current best direction, reduces uncertainty about a core profile/aggregation design choice, and creates a useful RNA-only multiprofile baseline before investing in multimodal fusion.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile RNA with PCA and avgpool (config_002) substantially outperforms singleprofile RNA PCA and image-only ResNet, making multiprofile RNA the most promising branch. The key unresolved question in that branch is whether transformer aggregation can improve on avgpool. config_003 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer, cleanly isolating the effect of profile aggregation while preserving the promising RNA PCA multiprofile setup. This is a high-value exploitation step before moving to more complex multimodal configurations.

The best current result is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (0.591 acc / 0.573 F1), while image-only ResNet single is weak (0.208 acc / 0.172 F1). It is unclear whether the multiprofile avgpool gain is specific to RNA or whether image can provide useful signal under the same profile/aggregation setting. config_011 tests image-only ResNet with multiprofile avgpool, isolating the profile/aggregation effect for the image modality before introducing fusion. This is a simple, controlled extension of the promising setting and reduces uncertainty about whether image is worth including in later multimodal experiments, making it a high-information use of the next budget.

RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool and PCA is currently the strongest setting, clearly outperforming singleprofile RNA and transformer aggregation, while image-only models are weak. The main remaining uncertainty is whether a learned RNA encoder can improve over PCA under the same profile and aggregation. config_005 tests only the RNA encoder by replacing pca_n2000 with scvi_n200 while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, isolating the representation effect. This is the best next use of budget because it avoids changing multiple factors, reduces uncertainty about RNA representation, and will inform whether future multimodal experiments should build on a stronger RNA backbone.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool and scvi_n200 (config_005, acc 0.6501, F1 0.6275), and avgpool already outperformed transformer for PCA multiprofile RNA (config_002 vs config_003). The key uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can help or harm the stronger scvi representation. config_006 tests this with a minimal one-factor change from the current best RNA configuration, clarifying whether avgpool or transformer should be preferred before moving to more complex multimodal designs.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 perform best, with avgpool and transformer aggregation giving similar high accuracy (~0.65) and F1. The main remaining uncertainty is whether the scgpt RNA representation can match or exceed scvi_n200 under the same favorable multiprofile/avgpool setting. config_008 tests this by changing only the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt, isolating the representation effect. This is the best next experiment because it is both potentially high-performing and informative, while avoiding confounding changes to image encoder, fusion, or aggregation before deciding whether multimodal configurations are worthwhile.

RNA multiprofile scvi is currently the strongest direction, while image-only ResNet50 is weak even with multiprofile avgpool. The key uncertainty is whether the image modality can become useful with a stronger image representation before spending budget on multimodal fusion. config_014 changes only the image encoder from ResNet50 to ImageNet ViT-L while keeping multiprofile and avgpool, making it directly comparable to config_011. It tests whether image representation quality is the bottleneck; if ViT substantially improves image-only performance, multimodal ViT configurations become more promising, otherwise the search can focus on RNA-only improvements. This isolates one important design choice and avoids confounding image encoder and fusion effects.

RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 is the strongest direction so far (avgpool 0.650, transformer 0.653), while image-only models are much weaker (resnet avgpool 0.328, ViT avgpool 0.332). The key uncertainty is whether adding image features can improve the best RNA-based model through fusion. config_031 tests this by adding ResNet50 image features to the near-best scvi_n200 multiprofile avgpool RNA setup with weighted fusion, which can downweight the weak image if it is unhelpful. This is the best next experiment because it directly probes the major untested modality/fusion decision on the strongest RNA base while avoiding an additional untested image transformer aggregation.
